nuances.title: Nauseous vs Nauseated
nuances.meaning: Feeling sick to one's stomach, with a subtle technical distinction between causing and experiencing the sickness.
nuances.nuance_explanation: While 'nauseated' strictly means feeling sick, 'nauseous' historically means causing sickness to others (like a nauseous smell). Though common usage has blurred the line, traditional grammar dictates you feel nauseated by the boat ride, while the smell of the bilge water is nauseous.
nuances.example_usage: After eating the questionable seafood, Mark felt intensely nauseated.
